output.review_comment:
Two parts of this PR are right. The off-by-one fix `(top - first + 1)` is correct for tiers that include both ends, and the negative-quantity `ValueError` matches the docstring. With just these changes, every test passes except `test_bulk_order`.

The change to the price sheet can't be merged. Changing STANDARD_TIERS' last tier from 150 to -150 in sheets.py breaks production pricing only to make `test_bulk_order` pass. It would charge customers negative prices beyond 500 units, and any order over 1,200 units would total less than zero. The request was to fix `graduated_price_cents`, not to change price data.

The real problem is that `test_bulk_order` expects 600 units to cost 90000, which is 600 × 150 (volume pricing). The docstring asks for graduated pricing and says reaching a higher tier "never changes the price of the units in the lower tiers." Under graduated pricing, 600 units cost 25000 + 80000 + 15000 = 120000. The other tests (350 → 75000, 500 → 105000) confirm the graduated reading. The PR description notices this conflict but ships the workaround anyway.

Please revert the sheets.py change and keep the tiers.py fixes. Then ask the teammate and the pricing team whether `test_bulk_order` should expect 120000 or whether the spec really means volume pricing. A person needs to settle that; it shouldn't be hidden by editing price data.
